intro: An operating system and the apps built into it, a horror game, eleven IT certifications and a YouTube channel: what RoYoshi builds, designs and knows.

paragraphs: RoYoshi makes whole things, from the code to the logo: a Linux desktop with a look of its own and the apps built into it, and a multiplayer horror game with its own website.

He programs The Far Backrooms and designs its game, levels, website, logos and promotional art, together with co-creator ₘₐᵣᵢᵢₖᵧᵤ. He builds FE-XicoOS on Fedora, and drew its green top hat and the FE-Xico Doctor badge you see on this page himself.
Behind the projects are eleven IT certifications from CompTIA and Cisco, covering support, networking, Linux and security.

groups.title: FE-XicoOS and its apps
groups.note: FE-Xico UpdateR and FE-Xico Doctor are separate repositories, and both are built into every FE-XicoOS image.

repos.name: FE-XicoOS
summary: An independently built Linux desktop on Fedora, for gaming, customising and a desktop with a look of its own. The whole system updates as one image (Fedora bootc), so an update either applies completely or not at all, and the previous version stays one restart away.
It runs KDE Plasma 6 and is in active development on Fedora 45. It is not a supported release yet.
inside: FE-Xico Aurora, one theme for the whole desktop: Plasma style, colours, icons, sounds, login screen, boot splash and wallpapers, in black with green and magenta
LaunchX, an optional application launcher of its own, next to KDE's
Gaming tools: Steam, MangoHud, vkBasalt, Gamescope and ProtonPlus
Everyday apps: Dolphin, Foot, LibreWolf, Bazaar, Bottles, Haruna, nomacs, Papers and Notepad Next
Flatpak, Distrobox, Podman and Homebrew for installing more

repos.name: FE-Xico UpdateR
summary: The update app of FE-XicoOS. It shows whether the system is up to date, gets a new system image ready, and explains restarting and rolling back in plain words. It never restarts the computer by itself, and it works with a keyboard, mouse, touch screen or game controller.
It began as a fork of Bazzite Updater by Robert French and contributors, and is now a project of its own that still reviews and takes in improvements from it.

repos.name: FE-Xico Doctor
summary: A health check for FE-XicoOS. It looks at the parts of the system that tend to go wrong (updates, services, graphics drivers, controllers, storage, Flatpaks, network and logs) and says what each finding means and what you can do about it.
It only looks: it never needs root, never changes anything, never goes online and never uploads anything. Reports can be shared with personal details such as names, addresses and keys replaced.

repos.name: The Far Backrooms
summary: A browser-first multiplayer survival-horror game, and a love letter to internet horror as a whole, with The Backrooms as its poster child. You wander the yellow rooms of Level 0 while the Hound and the Smiler hunt you, and everyone in a session meets the same monsters.

The browser draws the level with PixiJS, and a Node.js server runs the monsters and connects the players. It is in active development, built in stages; the current one, 2F, gives the monsters shared intelligence that works only from what they have actually seen.

certifications.note: Eleven certifications: four from CompTIA, three from Cisco, and the four that CompTIA awards for holding its certifications together.

certs.name: CompTIA A+
certs.scope: Hardware, operating systems, networking basics and troubleshooting: the groundwork of IT support.

certs.name: CompTIA Network+
certs.scope: Designing, running and troubleshooting wired and wireless networks.

certs.name: CompTIA Security+
certs.scope: Threats, secure architecture, security operations and responding to incidents.

certs.name: CompTIA Linux+
certs.scope: Running Linux systems: storage, services, security, scripting and troubleshooting.

certs.name: CCST IT Support
certs.scope: Helping people with their computers: hardware, software, accounts and the help desk.

certs.name: CCST Networking
certs.scope: Network basics: addressing, devices, services and finding what's wrong.

certs.name: CCST Cybersecurity
certs.scope: Security principles, network and endpoint security, vulnerability assessment and incident handling.
